message.content:
**United States – Gini coefficient (most recent estimate)**  

| Year | Gini coefficient (after‑tax & transfers) | Source |
|------|------------------------------------------|--------|
| 2021 | **≈ 0.41** | OECD, *Income inequality* database (latest published data) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (maximum inequality). A value of 0.41 indicates a moderate level of income inequality in the U.S., comparable to many other high‑income OECD countries.

> **Notes on the figure**  
> * The OECD figure is based on national accounts and household survey data, adjusted for taxes and transfers.  
> * Other sources (e.g., World Bank, U.S. Census Bureau) report slightly different numbers (e.g., 0.394 for 2019 in the World Bank data). The differences arise from variations in methodology, data coverage, and the year of the underlying surveys.  
> * The most recent OECD data available is for 2021; newer estimates may be released in the coming months.

If you need the Gini coefficient for a specific year or a different methodology (pre‑tax, household‑level, etc.), let me know!
